title: Honest Intervals for Policy Value under Guaranteed Recording with Learned Continuation

Delivered contribution specializes established shadow representer inference and monitoring projections to an exactly normalized, known diagonal sequential experiment; budget equivalences characterize estimator tuning, and the minimax converse perturbs only a low mode while the slower polynomial upper rate below s+t=1 lacks a corresponding nonparametric hardness result.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery established a normalized two-stage technical benchmark with learned continuation, distinct efficiency bounds, and three arbitrary-envelope inference regimes, but the authoritative field review capped its contribution at incremental (5.3 < 7.4). A false concentration inequality printed in the primary source was replaced through a scoped author-D repair by Pinelis Theorem3.4; independent review verified the bound and unchanged assumptions, rates, and ten-node reverse closure. The low-smoothness minimax gap, nonnumeric risk constants and practical validation remain open; no F-stage or Lean certification, promotion, presentation, or git commit occurred.
tldr: Every known vanishing common policy-tail envelope yields an explicit consistent estimator and shrinking honest intervals for the causal value under guaranteed first recording, with all nuisances, including the continuation, learned. The finite optimized budget gives the risk scale \(\mathcal A_n=n^{-1/2}(1+\mathcal B_n)\). Bounded \(L^{1-s}\omega(L)\) certifies conservative honest root-length intervals and, at the legal exponent-eight calibration, matched root-order minimax risk. Convergence \(L^{1-s}\omega(L)\to0\) certifies asymptotically exact Wald inference. Polynomial envelopes have conservative root-length coverage at \(s+t\geq1\) and Wald coverage at \(s+t>1\); below one the tighter balanced upper rate remains available, with its minimax gap unresolved. The positive results stay in the normalized diagonal two-stage benchmark, without a calibrated clinical claim.
gap: One-time shadow representer necessity and natural-recording OPE do not characterize feasible inference for a family of reward-adaptive guaranteed-recording policies whose loading contains an unknown continuation. The first missing proof step is a legal joint recording/continuation lower experiment compared with conditional-learning upper bounds, rather than another canonical-gradient calculation.
fill: The bracket theorem supplies a nonoracle sufficient region and a score-channel obstruction, while the first-class open question targets a matched sequential tail budget or a sharper honest bracket. The supporting interval and gradient lemmas calibrate the upper construction; they are not independent novelty claims.
